title: Microsoft Teams: meeting policy setting for profanity filtering in transcripts
summary: The briefing accurately reports the default masking behaviour, organiser-policy scope, controls and rollout information. It correctly flags the PowerShell reference's release caveat and unpublished licensing; the controls table should also cover policy assignment and the reported absence of a tenant-wide master switch.

claims.claim: Teams adds a meeting policy controlling profanity masking in live and saved meeting transcripts.
claims.quote: Teams administrators will be able to use a meeting policy to control whether profane words are masked in live transcription and saved meeting transcripts.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; rationales: risk and impact
claims.claim: Transcript profanity filtering is on by default and preserves existing masking behaviour.
claims.quote: The setting will be on by default, preserving the current transcript-masking behavior unless an administrator changes the assigned policy.

claims.claim: No administrator action is required to preserve current behaviour.
claims.quote: No action is required to preserve current behavior.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; controls[0].scope and note
claims.claim: The meeting organiser's assigned policy determines transcript filtering for their scheduled meetings.
claims.quote: The meeting organizer's assigned policy determines the behavior for the meeting.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Turning filtering off allows previously masked words to appear in both live and saved transcripts for affected scheduled meetings.
claims.quote: If an administrator turns filtering off for the policy assigned to a meeting organizer, words that would otherwise be masked can appear in both the live and saved transcript for that organizer's scheduled meetings.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; controls[2].note
claims.claim: Each participant's live-caption profanity preference is unchanged by the transcript setting.
claims.quote: Each participant's live-caption profanity preference; live captions continue to use the participant's existing setting.

claims.where: controls[3]; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Organisers and co-organisers have no per-meeting override of transcript filtering.
claims.quote: Organizers and co-organizers do not receive a per-meeting override.

claims.claim: The change adds no organiser-level control separate from assigned meeting policy.
claims.quote: This change does not add an organizer-level control and does not change each participant's live-caption profanity preference.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The filtering control is in Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting settings > Recording and transcription > Filter out profane words in live transcription.
claims.quote: A new Filter out profane words in live transcription setting will be available in the applicable Teams meeting policy under Meeting settings > Recording and transcription.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy accepts -Identity and -FilterProfanityInTranscript Enabled or Disabled to manage filtering.
claims.quote:
Controls whether meeting transcripts filter profanity.
Possible values are:
- Enabled: Filters profanity from the meeting transcript.
- Disabled: Does not filter profanity from the meeting transcript.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The cmdlet reference still warns that the filtering setting has no effect until the feature is fully released.
claims.quote: This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect.

claims.claim: The documented default for FilterProfanityInTranscript is Enabled.
claims.quote:
### -FilterProfanityInTranscript
| Type: | String |
| Default value: | Enabled |

claims.claim: Transcripts are stored together with meeting recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint storage.
claims.quote: Transcripts are stored together with meeting recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint storage.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether downstream Copilot recap processing uses masked or unmasked text for this setting.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams transcript profanity filtering Copilot recap masked unmasked'; 'site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams "profanity" "Copilot"'. Opened meeting-transcription-captions, copilot-teams-transcription and teams-admin; no passage specifies downstream masking.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Teams Administrator can manage meeting policies through Teams admin center and associated PowerShell controls.
claims.quote: Everything in the Microsoft Teams admin center and associated PowerShell controls, including: - Manage meetings, including meeting policies, configurations, and conference bridges.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Teams Communications Administrator can manage meeting policies through Teams admin center and PowerShell.
claims.quote: Teams Communications Administrator | Manage calling and meetings features within the Teams service. | Manage meetings, including meeting policies, configurations, and conference bridges.

claims.claim: The cited Learn documentation does not name a role specifically for this profanity-filter setting.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams FilterProfanityInTranscript Filter out profane words in live transcription administrator licensing captions override'. Opened Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, using-admin-roles and teams-admin; the parameter has no setting-specific role requirement.

claims.claim: This setting changes transcript word masking rather than introducing an autonomous action capability.
claims.quote: Teams administrators will be able to use a meeting policy to control whether profane words are masked in live transcription and saved meeting transcripts.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends confirming the business need and reviewing compliance policies and transcript requirements before disabling filtering.
claims.quote: Before turning filtering off, confirm the business need and review whether the change aligns with your organization's compliance policies and transcript requirements.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends notifying compliance, legal and helpdesk teams that saved transcripts may contain previously masked profanity.
claims.quote: Notify compliance, legal, and helpdesk teams that saved transcripts may contain profane words that were previously masked.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating internal transcript guidance if the organisation changes default policy behaviour.
claims.quote: Update internal transcript guidance if your organization changes the default policy behavior.

claims.claim: The transcription toggle is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one.
Toggle Transcription On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true or $false manages transcription.
claims.quote:
To manage meeting transcription using PowerShell, use the -AllowTranscription parameter in Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy.
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowTranscription $true

claims.claim: The existing Transcription policy setting allows or prevents transcription rather than configuring profanity masking.
claims.quote: Transcription is both a per-organizer and per-user policy setting. For meetings and events to include transcripts, the organizer must have this setting turned on. The user who starts the recording or transcript must also have this setting turned on.

claims.claim: The Teams admin release notes say users can change their live-caption profanity preference in settings.
claims.quote: Users who have already set their preference will keep their current setting. As a result, some users may begin seeing unfiltered profanity in live captions by default after this rollout. Users can update this preference in settings at any time.

claims.claim: No administrator UI or API controlling each participant's live-caption profanity preference is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams captions profanity preference administrator PowerShell Graph policy'; 'Teams live captions profanity filtering admin policy override per meeting tenant'. Opened meeting-transcription-captions, Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and teams-admin; no admin profanity-preference control.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Licensing for this specific setting is not yet published, so the licensing model is unknown rather than included.
claims.quote: Searched: '"FilterProfanityInTranscript" license pricing meter'; 'Teams meeting transcripts profanity filtering licensing pricing billing'. Read MC1478003 and the roadmap; opened Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, meeting-transcription-captions and Teams Premium licensing; no setting-specific licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a meter for this setting.
claims.quote: Searched: '"FilterProfanityInTranscript" license pricing meter'; 'Teams meeting transcripts profanity filtering licensing pricing billing'. Read MC1478003 and the roadmap; opened Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and Teams Premium licensing; no meter for this setting.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a price for this setting.
claims.quote: Searched: '"FilterProfanityInTranscript" license pricing meter'; 'Teams meeting transcripts profanity filtering licensing pricing billing'. Read MC1478003 and the roadmap; opened Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and Teams Premium licensing; no setting-specific price.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no separate tenant-wide master switch for transcript profanity filtering.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams transcript profanity filtering tenant wide master switch organizer meeting override FilterProfanityInTranscript'. Read MC1478003; opened Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, meeting-transcription-captions and teams-admin; only meeting-policy filtering documented.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The Global meeting policy supplies the default for users without another policy assignment, and custom policies can be assigned instead.
claims.quote: To apply changes to all users in your organization who don't have an existing policy assignment, use the Global policy. To exclude certain users from the global policy, create and assign a custom meeting policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Meeting policies can be assigned to specific users using the assignment steps on the transcription page.
claims.quote: To specific users: Select your policy, select Manage users > Assign users, enter the names of specific users in the search bar, select Add, and then select Apply.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Meeting policies can be assigned to groups using the assignment steps on the transcription page.
claims.quote: To groups: Select the Group policy assignment tab, select Add, enter the group name, select the policy name, and then select Apply.

claims.claim: The cited Learn pages do not document the admin-center location of the new filtering setting as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: 'site:learn.microsoft.com "Filter out profane words in live transcription"'. Opened meeting-transcription-captions, Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and teams-admin; none gives this UI path. The supplied MC1478003 does give the setting's location.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The controls table covers every control the checklist asks administrators to configure and every control the prose reports as absent.
claims.quote: Assign that policy only to named users or groups, using the assignment steps on the Learn transcription page. / Microsoft documents no tenant-wide master switch for it
